{{nihongo|'''Mito Shrine'''|御刀神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kashima-ku|Q24895757|qid=Q24895757}}, {{ill|Minamisōma|Q642094|qid=Q642094}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}. {{nihongo|'''Mito Shrine'''|御刀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].
Its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=old ranking}} was village shrine. It is one of eight Engishiki-listed shrines in Namekata District{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=of Engishiki}}.

== Enshrined deity ==
* Enshrines {{ill|Futsunushi|lt=Futsunushi-no-Kami|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286}}.
** The Sōma-domain history '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōsōshi}}' says Susanoo-no-Mikoto, but shrine tradition says this may be a record error confusing the deity of '''Yasaka Shrine''', a precinct shrine of Mito Shrine.

== Origin ==
It is said that in the era of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}}, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}} campaigned eastward, the deity was invited here. In {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} 5 ({{ill|905|Q24239|qid=Q24239}}), Mito Shrine was listed among 100 Engishiki shrines of {{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}} as a shrine with spiritual efficacy for protection of the state. In {{ill|Kangi|Q1194200|qid=Q1194200}} 1 (1229), the Namekata clan rebuilt shrine buildings and donated sacred fields; in {{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} 2 ({{ill|1712|Q6871|qid=Q6871}}), lord {{ill|Sōma Takatane|Q8515901|qid=Q8515901}} of {{ill|Sōma Nakamura Domain|Q844079|qid=Q844079}} donated 5 koku 3 shō. It was thus revered by both domain lords and local people. In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 11 it was designated village shrine.

The enshrined deity is traditionally identified as martial deity Futsunushi-no-Kami of {{ill|Katori Jingū|Q372380|qid=Q372380}} in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}. As seen in place name "Kenmiya" and shrine name, it is a shrine of the "sword," and records say the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} is an "ancient sword of a thousand years."

Standing near the sea amid rice fields, Mito Shrine was hit by the great tsunami of the {{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994}} {{ill|March 11|Q2398|qid=Q2398}} {{ill|2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|Q36204|qid=Q36204}}. The sacred grove remained, but torii, shrine buildings, and precinct shrines were swept away, and many nearby parishioner homes were also lost. After the disaster, restoration projects were carried out with support from shrine offices of various prefectures; with backing from {{ill|Hokkaido Prefectural Shrine Association|Q135249444|qid=Q135249444}} and {{ill|Shitaya Shrine|Q11361339|qid=Q11361339}} in
